summary: Shows regex_replace examples with backreferences, named groups, simple removal, and multiline comment-out, and warns to anchor patterns like ^(.*)$ to avoid double replacements.
questions: How do I replace text using a regex in Ansible?
How do I use named groups in regex_replace?
How do I comment out matching lines with regex_replace?
Why does regex_replace with (.*) replace twice?

answer_card.title: Replacing text with regex_replace
answer_card.answer_md:
```jinja
{{ 'ansible' | regex_replace('^a.*i(.*)$', 'a\\1') }}           # 'able'
{{ 'localhost:80' | regex_replace('^(?P<host>.+):(?P<port>\\d+)$', '\\g<host>, \\g<port>') }}
{{ 'localhost:80' | regex_replace(':80') }}                      # 'localhost'
{{ text | regex_replace('(?im)^(.ar)$', '#\\1') }}
```

When matching the whole string with `*`, anchor it: `^(.*)$`. A bare `(.*)` can also match the trailing empty string on some Python versions, causing two replacements.
